dedupe_keys.name: hubverse data standards and r python tools for collaborative modelling hubs

description: The hubverse is a set of open data standards and software for running collaborative modelling hubs, where many teams submit forecasts or scenario projections in one agreed format that can be validated, combined into ensembles, evaluated and visualised. It is developed by the Consortium of Infectious Disease Modeling Hubs, which works with national and international health agencies such as the US and European Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Coverage: generic tools, used by hubs in the United States, Europe and elsewhere; the site lists the hubs built on it. A hub is defined by configuration files that follow the hubverse schema, stating tasks, targets, locations and output types such as quantiles, samples or probabilities; R packages hubAdmin, hubValidations, hubData, hubEnsembles, hubEvals and hubVis, with dashboards, handle set-up, submission checks, data access, ensembling, scoring and plots. Format and access: open-source packages and templates on GitHub with documentation; free. Licence: open-source licences set per package on GitHub (not each checked here); hubs built with it, such as FluSight, use MIT. Caveats: the tools assume tabular model outputs in a hub repository and are designed around epidemic forecasting, so other domains must adapt the task definitions. Simulation uses: organising multi-model forecasts and scenario projections for capacity planning and emergency response, for example hospital demand. Related records: the CDC forecast hubs (data-cdc-respiratory-forecast-hubs) are built on the hubverse.
